rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prophets know that every being in the heavens and earth submits to God willingly or unwillingly and returns to Him.
rows.anchor: tav‘an ve kerhen Allah’a inkıyâdını bilen ve cümlesi Allah’a ircâ‘olunacak olan enbiyâ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets never seek a claim or way beyond obedience to God and surrender to the truth; they call people to become God-nurtured through His teaching.
rows.anchor: enbiyâ hiçbir zaman Allah dininden, Allah’a itaatten, Hakk’a teslimiyetten başka bir talepte

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı derives rabbānī from rabb or rabbān, meaning a lord or educator; he points to the later description of many rabbiyyūn with a prophet.
rows.anchor: “Rabbânî”, “rabb”a, veya mürebbî mânasına “rabbân”a mensubdur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God wants to remove burdensome obligations and lighten people's accountability because humanity was created weak.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ sizden ağır teklifleri kaldırıp mes’ûliyetinizi tahfif etmek ister. Zira insan zayıf olarak halk edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Legislation may not permit following lust, but it may not impose excessive severity or oppression either.
rows.anchor: bâb-ı teşrî‘de şehvete tâbi‘olmak câiz olmadığı gibi şiddet ü tazyik de câiz değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He treats the easing as an answer to the prayer against burdens and links it with scripture's repeated principle of ease and removal of hardship.
rows.anchor: dualarının bir eser-i icâbeti vardır ki

rows.speaker: Peygamber
rows.claim: A Prophetic hadith says he was sent with the upright, easy, and lenient way; Elmalılı cites it as affirming relief in religion.
rows.anchor: جِئْتُكُمْ بِالحَْنِيفِي َّةِ ال َّسهْلَةِ ال َّسمْحَةِ hadîs-i nebevîsi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People cannot bear severity and need relief; Islam came to grant that relief, contrary to the assumption that humans are strong.
rows.anchor: İnsanlar zannettikleri gibi kavî bir mahluk değildirler. Şiddete dayanamazlar, tahfîfe muhtaçtırlar ve dîn-i İslâm onlara bu tahfîfi bahşetmek için gelmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marriage rules and dealings should be made easier, avoiding undue restrictions that could open the way to fornication or misuse.
rows.anchor: nikâh hususunda da teşdîdât gösterilmemeli, zinâya ve sû’-i isti‘mâle meydan vermemek için ahkâm ve mu‘âmelât-ı nikâh teshil olunmalıdır.

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says eight verses in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ are better for this community than everything on which the sun rises and sets; Elmalılı lists them.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas hazretlerinden mervîdir ki şöyle demiştir: Sûre-i Nisâ’da sekiz âyet bu ümmet için güneşin üzerine doğduğu ve battığı şeylerin hepsinden hayırlıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He transitions to the next address because marriage has a particular connection with financial ability and the acquisition and management of wealth.
rows.anchor: nikâhın kudret-i mâliye ile bir alâka-i mahsûsası bulunmasına mebnî emvâlin kesb ü tasarrufuna müte‘allik

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is a fully reliable guide revealed in truth, setting out people's rights before God and one another and showing justice, truth, and sincerity without falsehood or deviation.
rows.anchor: bu kitâb-ı ekmeli, bu Kur’ân-ı azîmü’ş-şân’ı hak ile, Hak teâlâ’nın insanlar üzerinde insanların ferden veya cem‘an yekdiğeri beynindeki hukūkun künhünü muhtevî

words: لِتَحْكُمَ بَيْنَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِمَآ أَرَىٰكَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to settle every doctrinal or practical dispute by God's truth and absolute revelation, giving everyone equally the right they deserve.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın sana gösterdiği ilm-i hak ve vahy-i mutlak ile hükmedesin.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book's central purpose is to establish a basis for judging; the Prophet's distinctive task is to use revelation and its knowledge as the sole standard where revelation has spoken.
rows.anchor: Peygamber’in min tarafillah vârid olan vahyi ve vahiyden mütehassıl ilmi müstakillen medâr-ı hükm ittihaz etmesi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other proofs are only outward appearances, whereas revelation is necessary knowledge corresponding to the truth's essence.
rows.anchor: delâil-i sâire sırf zâhirî olduğu hâlde vahiy künh-i hakka muntabık bir ilm-i zarûrîdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A judge must pursue truth rather than personal preference and must never decide against a right he knows with certainty; the verse validates knowledge only when it is witnessed certainty, not opinion or ijtihād.
rows.anchor: Burada ilm-i hâkimin muteber olduğuna bir delil vardır. Fakat bunun bir re’y ü ictihad değil, bir ilm-i şuhûdî olması şarttır.

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Ömer
rows.claim: Umar warns people not to call their own opinion something God showed them: that wording denotes revelation particular to the Prophet, while their opinions remain conjecture.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ömer demiştir ki “Allah’ın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judges cannot rule from mere opinion or conviction; they must investigate evidentiary means and follow what those proofs establish.
rows.anchor: hâkimler mücerred re’y ü kanaatleriyle hükmedemezler. Esbâb ve vesâit-i sübûtiye taharrîsine ve onların delâletine ittibâ‘a mecburdurlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the goal is to reach the truth, a judge may never rule against a fact known through witnessed certainty.
rows.anchor: maksad-ı aslî hakka isabet olduğundan hâkimin ilm-i şühûdî ile mâlumu olan bir hususta ilmi hilâfına hükmetmesi asla câiz olmaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not defend traitors or feud against innocent people on their behalf, even if the innocent belong to another community; do not act as their lawyer.
rows.anchor: kim olursa olsun, velevse ümmetinden bulunsun hâinleri müdafaa için berî olanlara velevse millet-i âhardan olsun husumet etme.

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators agree that the passage was revealed about the Banū Ubayriq affair; Kirmānī specifies Tuʿma ibn Ubayriq of Banū Ẓafar ibn al-Ḥārith.
rows.anchor: Bu âyetlerin Benî Übeyrık vak‘ası hakkında nâzil olduğunda müfessirînin ittifâkı nakl olunuyor. Ebû Hayyân’ın nakline göre Kirmânî demiştir

rows.speaker: İbn Bahr
rows.claim: Ibn Bahr says the verses concern hypocrites and are connected to 4:88; Elmalılı says this need not conflict with the consensus because Tuʿma, called Bashīr, was a hypocrite.
rows.anchor: İbn Bahr demiştir ki münafıklar hakkında nâzil oldu

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Rāzī says commentators agree that most of these verses were revealed about Tuʿma ibn Ubayriq, though reports differ over the incident's details.
rows.anchor: Bunun için Râzî ıtlâkı üzere der ki: Bu âyetlerin ekserîsi Tu‘me b. Übeyrık hakkında nâzil olduğunda müfessirîn müttefiktir.

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: One reported version says Tuʿma stole armor and, when pursued, blamed a Jew.
rows.anchor: Birisi Tu‘me zırhlı bir gömlek sirkat etmiş, talep olununca sirkati bir Yahudîye atfetmiş.

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: A second version says the armor had been entrusted to Tuʿma, who denied taking it when asked; a third says he accused the Jew when questioned.
rows.anchor: İkincisi: Zırh kendisine vedî‘a bırakılmış, şâhid de yokmuş, talep olununca inkâr etmiş. Üçüncüsü: Talep edildiği zaman Yahudînin çaldığını iddia etmiş.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı prefers the majority's account: Tuʿma stole armor from neighbor Qatāda ibn Nuʿmān, hid it in a flour sack, and its trail led to Jew Zayd ibn Samīn, who said Tuʿma had left it with him.
rows.anchor: Ekser müfessirînin muhtârına göre rivayetlerin hâsılı şudur: Ensar meyânında Benî Zafer’den Tu‘me b. Übeyrık nâmında birisi komşusu Katâde b. Numan’dan bir gece bir un dağarcığı içinde bir dir‘-zırh- çalmış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In that account, Banū Ẓafar vouched for Tuʿma, asked the Prophet to acquit him and blame the Jew, and urged defense of Tuʿma; revelation identified the guilty and innocent party.
rows.anchor: Tu‘me’yi müdafaa edip Müslümanlık nâmına Yahudîlerle mücadele eylemesini rica eylemişler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: According to the preferred account, the Prophet initially leaned toward defending Tuʿma on the basis of his oath and the tribe's testimony, but revelation exposed the traitor and innocent party.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah da zâhirde Müslüman olan Tu‘me’nin yeminine ve bunların şehadetine binâen öyle yapmak istemiş, bunun üzerine min tarafillah bu âyetler nâzil olmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rather than repent, Tuʿma fled to Mecca and apostatized; after further thefts and expulsion, accounts say he died under a collapsing wall or was killed after robbing a merchant caravan, and 4:115 then came down regarding apostates' fate.
rows.anchor: Tu‘me hakka teslim olup tevbekâr olacak yerde Mekke’ye kaçmış ve irtidad etmiş.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the occasion of revelation, the traitors are Tuʿma and his helpers; generally the wording applies to unjust and immoral people like them.
rows.anchor: sebeb-i nüzûle nazaran “hâinîn”den murad bu Tu‘me ve buna mu‘âvenet edenler, sûret-i umûmiyede de bu gibi haksızlar ve ahlâksızlardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The responsibility of judges, witnesses, and advocates is grave; even an unwitting inclination toward a traitor against an innocent person, misled by outward evidence, is itself a fault.
rows.anchor: hâkimin velev bilmeyerek olsun velevse esbâb-ı zâhireye aldanarak olsun bir hâin lehine meyledip berî’ü’z-zimme olan bir kimseye husumet etmesi haddizâtında bir kusur olduğunu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God protected the Prophet from this fault and granted knowledge of the unseen, after his inclination to defend Tuʿma based on outward Islam and his tribe's request and testimony.
rows.anchor: İslâm-ı zâhirîye ve kavminin talep ve şehadetine binâen Tu‘me’yi müdafaaya meyletmiş olmasından dolayı Peygamber’i hatâdan sıyânet ederken

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to seek forgiveness precedes the other warnings, and God's being forgiving and merciful invites those who ask pardon.
rows.anchor: Allah mağfiret isteyenlere Gafûr, Rahîm’dir diye istiğfâra davet etmeden diğer ihtârâta geçmemiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although divine grace and prophetic wisdom protected him from error, the initial call to seek forgiveness signals a forceful reproach; the later mention of grace is offered as a favor to be acknowledged.
rows.anchor: evvelemirde istiğfâra davet edilmesi her hâlde bir itâb-ı belîği müş‘irdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning severely condemns knowingly aiding treachery and injustice, promoting wrong for gain, prejudice, or collusion, and judges who follow desire instead of right; it also urges repentance.
rows.anchor: haksızların haksızlıklarını bile bile zulm ü hıyanete mu‘âvenet edenlere ve

words: وَلَا تُجَٰدِلْ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخْتَانُونَ أَنفُسَهُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not argue or act as counsel for those who betray themselves, and do not judge on their testimony.
rows.anchor: Nefislerine hıyanet edenler tarafından veya onlardan dolayı mücadele etme, böylelerinin ne vekîl-i muhâmîsi ol ne şehadetleriyle hükmet.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Betraying oneself means self-deception: imagining one gains a benefit while actually bringing oneself harm; sin exposes the entrusted self to punishment, and siding with a traitor is also self-betrayal.
rows.anchor: “Nefsine Hıyanet” kendini aldatmak, bir menfaat celb ediyor zu‘muyla bir zarar getirmektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hawwān means intensely treacherous and athīm intensely sinful: someone who does not avoid betrayal or sin.
rows.anchor: “Havvân” pek hâin, “esîm” pek günahkâr, yani hıyanetten sakınmayan ve günahtan çekinmeyen demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic wording warns against persistence and habitual wrongdoing while encouraging repentance.
rows.anchor: Bu ifadede ısrar ve itiyaddan tahzir ve tevbeye bir teşvik vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage depicts a particular group among self-betrayers who secretly devise what God disapproves, hiding it from people but not from God, who is with them.
rows.anchor: Burada nefse hıyanetin bir suretini îzah ve nefislerine hıyanet edenlerden bir kısm-ı mahsûsun tasvîri vardır

words: يُبَيِّتُونَ مَا لَا يَرْضَىٰ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْلِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation derives tabyīt from baytūta: to plan or carry out a matter at night, in darkness.
rows.anchor: “Beytûtet”ten olduğuna göre bir işi geceleyin tedbir etmek, geceletmek, gece karanlığında yapmaktır.

words: يُبَيِّتُونَ مَا لَا يَرْضَىٰ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْلِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative derives tabyīt from bayt, composing and polishing a statement like a metrical verse or poem.
rows.anchor: “Beyt”ten olduğuna göre de bir sözü manzum bir beyit, bir şiir yapar gibi uğraşıp uydurmak

words: يُبَيِّتُونَ مَا لَا يَرْضَىٰ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْلِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such people devise bad ideas privately or in groups, meeting at night or polishing contrived accounts, then make plans God disapproves while fearing people more than God.
rows.anchor: Bu gibi kimseler de zihinlerinde veya aralarında fena fikirler tertip ederler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God encompasses everything they do, misses nothing, and will punish them in due course; their wrongdoing only deceives and betrays themselves.
rows.anchor: onlar ne yapıyorlarsa Allah hepsini muhîttir. Hiçbirini kaçırmaz, erinde gecinde cezâlarını verir

words: يُبَيِّتُونَ مَا لَا يَرْضَىٰ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْلِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since Tuʿma's would-be defenders belong among these plotters, Elmalılı turns the address toward them after describing their conduct.
rows.anchor: Tu‘me gibi hâinleri müdafaa ve himâye etmek isteyenler de bu gibiler meyânında bulunduğu için bu tasvir üzerine telvîn-i hitâb ile
